description.narrative: The Project aims to support Liquid Telecom Holding Limited (Liquid or the Company) at raising US$220 million in ZAR equivalent to be borrowed by their South African subsidiary Liquid Telecom South Africa (LTSA). IFC is providing up to ZAR 1,029 million as part of the Company's effort to strengthen its balance sheet structure. This will include the refinancing of Liquids existing ZAR debt and drawn portion of the US$ revolving credit facility, extending tenors and moving away from a single maturity, as well as potentially repurchasing a portion of its bond (the Project). The Project is taking place in a context where Liquid is undergoing a capital rebalancing exercise. Liquid is a strong Telco partner in South Africa and across the African continent. Since its establishment in 2004, Liquid has anchored the development of the broadband market in Africa with its presence across the region. The Project will help ensure the continuity of Liquids endeavor to bridge the connectivity gap in Africa and enhance the resilience of the fixed broadband market in its countries.

The Project is expected to increase Liquids capacity to enhance customer connections through last-mile connectivity. While this investment mainly consists of refinancing existing debt associated with activities in Sub-Saharan Africa, this will enable the Company to unlock more free cash flow for capital expansion plans across Africa over the next few years. Such expansion includes furthering Liquids fiber network and digital footprint of services across countries of operation. Beyond the Company, this project is expected to enhance the resilience of the broadband market in Africa by supporting a large player to face headwinds and continue its growth strategy which aims to increase broadband capacity for retail operators in the Pan-African markets including South Africa, Zimbabwe, Tanzania, Kenya, Zambia and DRC.
